iOS 27 will launch this fall and includes a new Apple Calendar feature I've been waiting years for: natural language input support when creating events.

iOS 27 brings natural language support to Apple Calendar event creation

I've used the Apple Calendar app for years, but there's always been one feature sitting at the top of my most-wanted list: natural language support.

The excellent third-party app Fantastical has long had powerful natural language features.

Fantastical lets you type all the details of a new event in one line, much like you'd speak them in everyday conversation. The app then automatically extracts important information like the time, location, and attendees, without requiring additional manual input.

Now, with the launch of iOS 27, Apple's own Calendar app is finally getting a similar feature.

Here's how Apple describes the feature on its official website:

I've been testing this new feature in the iOS 27 beta, and it works remarkably well.

If you type "3pm meeting," the event time will automatically change to 3pm. As for other information you may or may not want to include, relevant suggestions will appear at the top of the keyboard.

For example, if you type "coffee with Mark at Starbucks," you can tap the suggestions to add attendees and/or a location to the event, or leave them in the event title.

Bonus: Since the Calendar app also supports creating new reminders, this natural language system also applies to any reminders you create.

How important is natural language input for the Calendar app to you? Let us know in the comments.
